title: Biodiesel and Activated Carbon from Arabica Spent Coffee Grounds
author: Kusuma, Indartono, et al.

steps.title: Perform Soxhlet oil extraction
steps.instruction: Extract oil from 100 g dried spent coffee grounds using a Soxhlet extractor with 750 mL n‑hexane; run the extraction for 89.79 minutes, repeat the procedure 19 times, and calculate the average oil yield (18.14 % w/w of dried grounds) and solvent recovery (74.23 %).

substeps.instruction: Weigh 100 g of dried spent coffee grounds and place them in the Soxhlet extraction thimble.
Add 750 mL of n‑hexane to the extraction flask.
Assemble the Soxhlet apparatus and heat to reflux, allowing the extraction to proceed for 89.79 minutes.
Cool, collect the extracted oil, and measure the mass of oil obtained.
Repeat the entire extraction 19 times, recording the oil mass each run.
Average the oil yields to obtain 18.14 % (mass of oil / mass of dried grounds).
Determine the volume of n‑hexane recovered and calculate solvent recovery (74.23 %).

steps.title: Set up GC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the extracted coffee oil by GC‑MS using an Agilent 8890 gas chromatograph with autosampler coupled to an Agilent 59778 mass spectrometer; install an Agilent HP‑5MS capillary column (30 m × 0.25 mm i.d., 0.25 µm film), use helium as carrier gas, program the oven: start at 60 °C, ramp 15 °C/min to 175 °C, then 2 °C/min to 240 °C, hold 10 min; set detector temperature to 230 °C and injector temperature to 250 °C.

substeps.instruction: Install the HP‑5MS column (30 m × 0.25 mm i.d., 0.25 µm film) in the Agilent 8890 GC.
Connect helium as the carrier gas and set appropriate flow rate.
Program the oven temperature: 60 °C initial, increase 15 °C/min to 175 °C, then 2 °C/min to 240 °C, hold for 10 min.
Set the detector (MS) temperature to 230 °C and the injector temperature to 250 °C.
Load the oil sample into the autosampler vial and place it in the Agilent 8890 autosampler.
Start the GC‑MS run using the defined method.

steps.title: Measure biodiesel and carbon properties
steps.instruction: Determine biodiesel properties using the specified standards: density at 15 °C (ASTM D1298), kinematic viscosity at 40 °C (ASTM D445), acid value (AOCS Cd 3d‑63), saponification value (AOCS Ca 14‑56), iodine value (AOCS Cd 1‑25), oxidation stability (EN 14112), and higher heating value (ASTM D240‑02 2007). Determine activated‑carbon properties using ASTM methods: moisture content (ASTM D2867‑04), ash content (ASTM D2866‑94), volatile matter content (ASTM D5832‑98), and iodine number (ASTM D4607‑94).

substeps.instruction: Measure biodiesel density at 15 °C according to ASTM D1298.
Measure biodiesel kinematic viscosity at 40 °C according to ASTM D445.
Determine biodiesel acid value following AOCS Cd 3d‑63.
Determine biodiesel saponification value following AOCS Ca 14‑56.
Determine biodiesel iodine value following AOCS Cd 1‑25.
Assess biodiesel oxidation stability according to EN 14112.
Measure biodiesel higher heating value according to ASTM D240‑02 (2007).
Measure activated‑carbon moisture content per ASTM D2867‑04.
Measure activated‑carbon ash content per ASTM D2866‑94.
Measure activated‑carbon volatile matter per ASTM D5832‑98.
Determine activated‑carbon iodine number per ASTM D4607‑94.
